surfaces.part: gray metal top cap/frame of signboard
red signboard panel with cream Korean lettering

answer.evidence: The sign is a tall vertical panel seen face-on. The red board (rows 9-28) is a flat vertical face with cream lettering and a dark band at rows 17-18. The gray head at rows 1-6 is a lighter block with a highlight, but it ends in no front-edge line and has no eave shadow. It reads as a vertical cap or frame, not a horizontal top. Rows 7-8 are a dark outline gap. There is no ellipse, no roof or awning plane, and no contents. The 1-row base at row 30 is too thin to count as a top. The width profile is a constant 14 from rows 1-30, so nothing widens and narrows. This is a front elevation with no top surface.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a narrow standing sign: a dark red body with a lighter red lettering panel, white-ish 국밥 text, and a dark top and bottom cap. It has 11 visible tones per tile, close to kiosk-a (12) and above bus-shelter-a (6), though below vending-a (20). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no flat fills. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is tinted, dark red-brown beside the red body, matching the references' treatment. Shading on the red body looks like about 4 steps (highlight, mid, dark, deep), slightly fewer than the references' 5-6. The piece is small and simple, with little grain beyond the lettering and edge shading, so it reads somewhat thinner than vending-a, but it is on par with the shipped bus-shelter-a and kiosk-a. It would sit acceptably next to them.

surfaces.part: red signboard panel with cream lettering (front face)

answer.evidence: Rows 1-6 form a gray cap band with a highlight at rows 2-3, so it is lit like a horizontal surface. It ends in a darker front-edge line at row 6 (L=71 against L=113-132 above). Rows 7-8 are a dark eave shadow beneath it (L=17). Below that, the red panel on rows 9-28 is a 20-row vertical front face carrying the cream lettering, and rows 29-31 are a dark base. The cap's 6 rows are well over a 1-2 row rim, but the evidence is borderline: it could also be read as a front-facing header box.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small vertical sign with a dark red body, a lighter edge and highlight, a dark red-brown frame and light lettering. Its outline carries a red-brown tint rather than neutral black, and the measured 0% near-neutral dark edge pixels confirms this. It has 11 visible tones per tile, which is level with kiosk-a (12) and well above bus-shelter-a (6), only below vending-a (20). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no large flat fills; the red panel is broken up by the lettering, edge highlights and shading. It has about 4 ramp steps against roughly 5 on the references, which is slightly simpler but fits a thin sign prop. An artist would accept it next to these references without it looking flatter or more sticker-like.

surfaces.part: gray cap block on top of the sign
red sign panel with cream hangul text (front face)

answer.evidence: The column scan shows a gray cap band at rows 1-6. Rows 2-3 are lighter (L=202-231 at x=8) and rows 4-5 are mid-tone (L=113). Row 6 is a darker 1-row front-edge line (L=71), and rows 7-8 are very dark eave shadow (L=17). Below this is the front face: a red panel at rows 9-28 with cream text and a dark divider at rows 16-18, then a base strip at rows 29-30. The silhouette is a constant 14 px wide with no receding side face. The top band is a modest cap on a vertical sign, but it has a top band, an edge line and shadow, like the cabinet reference (top 5 + edge + eave). This is a borderline read, because the cap could also be a front-facing header.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small vertical sign: a dark red body with a lighter red-brown border, light '국밥' lettering, and a pale cap and base. Its 11 visible tones per tile sit between bus-shelter-a (6) and kiosk-a (12), below vending-a (20). Near-flat coverage is 0%, and dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is tinted dark red-brown rather than black. Shading is about 4 steps on the red body (border highlight, mid, dark, deep) against roughly 5 on the references. The sign face is mostly a smooth fill broken up by the lettering, so texture is only moderate and there is no grain or speckle. It is a simple single-tile prop and is not noticeably thinner than the bus shelter or kiosk. It would sit acceptably in the chipset, though it is a little less dense than vending-a.

surfaces.part: gray top cap of the sign

answer.evidence: The sign has a gray cap at rows 1-6 with a lighter highlight at rows 1-3. Row 6 is darker (L=71 against 113 above), which reads as a front-edge line. Rows 7-8 are very dark (L=17), which reads as eave shadow. Below that, the red panel with the text runs from row 9 to row 28 as the front face, about 22 rows with the shadow band. The cap is borderline: it could also be read as a header block, but the edge line plus the shadow fit evidence (a). There is no receding side face. The 2-row foot at rows 30-31 is a minor detail.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small red vertical sign with white 국밥 lettering, a dark red-brown border and a light highlight edge.
